description: NetFlow, IPFIX and sFlow received by xflow-exporter. The strip across the top says whether the data below can be trusted; the open rows answer the circuit and LAN questions; the collapsed rows carry diagnostic depth and do not query until opened. Flow export is sampled, so every packet and byte figure is an estimate scaled by the sampling rate -- take an exact volume from the device's SNMP interface counters. What flow export gives that SNMP cannot is the dimensions: AS, protocol, application, peer. Rollup sets the rate window; pick one at least twice the scrape interval or every panel reads empty. The composition panels rank rather than total, and Ranking coverage says how much of the traffic they account for.

panels.description: Every byte and packet figure on this dashboard has been multiplied by this rate, so it is the frame the volume numbers are read in. Flow counts are not multiplied. A domain that has declared no rate publishes no series, and its records were corrected by one.
panels.title: Sampling rate in force

panels.description: What share of the device's packets the entries of each table actually name. The denominator is the exporters family, the one family published without a Top-K bound, so it is a true device total. The shortfall is the withheld Top-K tail and the folded overflow together, and it bounds how much of the traffic every composition panel below can account for. Both sides are sampling-corrected, so the correction cancels and the ratio is exact even though its operands are estimates.
panels.title: Ranking coverage

panels.description: Sampling-corrected estimate of what the device is forwarding. An estimate: a transit invoice is settled against the device's SNMP interface counters, not against this. Needs the exporters module; without it this reads no data while the process is healthy.
panels.title: Link bitrate now

panels.description: Decode throughput, from the health family that carries no collector-module flag, so this is present on a default install where every traffic module is off. Records as the device exported them: a packet-sampling protocol observes flows rather than counting them, so this is never multiplied by the sampling rate.
panels.title: Flow records decoded

panels.description: How many of five conditions that would make every traffic panel below untrustworthy are true now: a device silent past the entry TTL, receiver drops, decode rejects other than a missing template, export sequence loss, and records folded at the entry bound. Each term is wrapped in a zero vector because this counts breached checks rather than measured traffic, so a zero here is a real reading rather than a fabricated one.

targets.expr:
(count(time() - xflow_last_flow_timestamp_seconds{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"} > 900) or vector(0))
+ (count(increase(xflow_receiver_dropped_packets_total[15m]) > 0) or vector(0))
+ (count(increase(xflow_decode_errors_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",reason!="missing_template"}[15m]) > 0) or vector(0))
+ (count(increase(xflow_sequence_missed_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[15m]) > 0) or vector(0))
+ (count(increase(xflow_aggregation_overflow_records_total[15m]) > 0) or vector(0))

panels.title: Trust checks failing

panels.description: Seconds since each device's last decoded record. Flow export is push, so there is no up-style reachability toward a sender and this is the only signal that a device has gone quiet. The warning line is the entry TTL its own alerting rule fires on, past which that device's entries start disappearing. A device that has never decoded has no series and no tile.
panels.title: Silence per device

panels.description: Up against down against what never leaves the LAN. Built on the country pair table and its documented private marker -- RFC 1918 and the IPv6 unique local range -- rather than a hand-written prefix regex, which would misread every IPv6 ULA flow as internet. That table is well inside the entry bound here, so this is a total rather than a ranking; the folded other series is excluded from both directions. Needs the countries module and a country database. Ingress-only observation is why the two directions are separate measurements rather than one figure counted twice. Sampled estimate.

targets.expr:
label_replace(sum(rate(xflow_country_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src_country="private",dst_country!="private",dst_country!="other"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8, "direction", "egress (LAN to internet)", "", "") or
label_replace(sum(rate(xflow_country_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",dst_country="private",src_country!="private",src_country!="other"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8, "direction", "ingress (internet to LAN)", "", "") or
label_replace(sum(rate(xflow_country_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src_country="private",dst_country="private"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8, "direction", "internal (LAN to LAN)", "", "")

panels.title: Circuit direction split

panels.description: Which machine is loading the uplink. LAN-to-LAN is excluded so east-west traffic does not inflate the figure. Ranks rather than totals: these are the biggest talkers, and a host below the Top-K cut is absent rather than zero. The cut is by byte volume, which is exactly the ordering this panel wants. Sampled estimate.

value.title: Filter the conversation tables to this address

panels.title: LAN hosts by outbound bits

panels.description: The same pairs a line chart would carry, sorted instead of overlaid, and ranked in bits rather than packets so a chatty small-packet flow does not outrank one filling the uplink. Observation is ingress-only, so the two directions of one conversation are separate rows and must not be read as a bidirectional total. Ranks rather than totals. Sampled estimate. Narrowed by the focus variable, which the tables' address links set.

targets.expr:
topk(15,
  sum by (src, dst) (rate(xflow_host_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"$focus"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8
  or
  sum by (src, dst) (rate(xflow_host_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",dst=~"$focus"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8
)

panels.title: Top conversations now
Who and what -- ranked right now

panels.description: Where the LAN's traffic goes, named by the AS organization database. The local side of the pair is AS 0 under ingress-only observation, so collapsing the pair to the one AS that exists halves the label and doubles the signal. An AS no lookup resolved keeps its bar under its bare number rather than being dropped by the join. Ranks rather than totals: the tail below the Top-K cut is withheld, not folded. Sampled estimate.

targets.expr:
topk(12, sum by (dst_asn) (rate(xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src_asn="0",dst_asn!="0"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8)
* on (dst_asn) group_left (as_name)
  (
    label_replace(label_join(label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "dst_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", " (AS", "organization", "asn"), "as_name", "$1)", "as_name", "(.+)")
    or
    label_replace(group by (dst_asn) (xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total) unless on (dst_asn) label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "dst_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", "AS$1", "dst_asn", "(.+)")
  )

panels.title: Internet peers by egress bits

panels.description: The mirror of the egress ranking, and its own panel rather than a second series: under ingress-only observation the two directions are different measurements, and a peer that is large inbound while absent outbound is the interesting case -- a CDN pushing, or somebody probing. Placed beside egress so an asymmetry is a visual comparison. Ranks rather than totals. Sampled estimate.

targets.expr:
topk(12, sum by (src_asn) (rate(xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",dst_asn="0",src_asn!="0"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8)
* on (src_asn) group_left (as_name)
  (
    label_replace(label_join(label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "src_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", " (AS", "organization", "asn"), "as_name", "$1)", "as_name", "(.+)")
    or
    label_replace(group by (src_asn) (xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total) unless on (src_asn) label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "src_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", "AS$1", "src_asn", "(.+)")
  )

panels.title: Internet peers by ingress bits

panels.description: Three label dimensions no legend string can carry, as one sortable column each: sorting by port groups every 443 row together and separates QUIC from TCP. The protocol lives here as a column, which is why there is no separate protocol-mix panel -- a share of this family would be fabricated while the family is truncated. Directional and ingress-only: this is what a service received on the observed direction. Ranks rather than totals. Sampled estimate.
panels.title: Top destination services

panels.description: The named application mix as ranked bars rather than near-flat lines. Deliberately not a pie: the tail below the Top-K cut is withheld rather than folded, so a percentage would assert a whole this family does not have. This family carries no address, so attributing an application to a machine means going to the service five-tuple table. Sampled estimate.
panels.title: Applications now

panels.description: What is being served on the campus. Two filters are deliberate heuristics: the destination is restricted to RFC 1918, and the port to four digits, which drops the ephemeral ports a reverse-direction record puts in the port label and with them any genuine listener above 9999. Read the protocol column -- for ICMP the port label is the type and code word rather than a port, so such a row is not a listening service. Ranks from a table whose cut is by byte volume, so a quiet listener can be withheld before it is ranked.
panels.title: Services reached inside the LAN

panels.description: Every RFC 1918 to RFC 1918 pair the observation point sees, to read against what the access policy is meant to permit. East-west never reaches the transit circuit and is buried under it in any unfiltered ranking, which is why it needs its own panel. The trailing test drops entries still held within the entry TTL whose rate over the window is zero, so only live pairs appear. Ranked from a Top-K table, so the absence of a pair is not proof it did not happen.

targets.expr:
topk(20,
  sum by (src, dst) (rate(xflow_host_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",src=~"$focus",dst=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8
  or
  sum by (src, dst) (rate(xflow_host_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",dst=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",dst=~"$focus"}[$rollup_interval])) * 8
) > 0

panels.title: East-west traffic across the LAN

panels.description: Flooded traffic hits every port in the VLAN and every wireless client individually, so its cost is per frame: this is the one composition panel correctly ranked by packets rather than bits. The selector covers 224.0.0.0/4 and the limited broadcast address. It cannot catch a subnet-directed broadcast, which no prefix test can distinguish from a host address. Packets are sampling-corrected.
panels.title: Broadcast and multicast destinations

panels.description: A QoS policy is a claim about proportions, so this shows proportions against an explicit denominator. The share is legitimate here only because this table holds far fewer entries than the entry bound -- it is complete rather than truncated -- and the same construction on an address-keyed family would fabricate a whole. A bar labelled with a bare number is a code point the exporter knows no class name for, which is by definition an unexpected marking: a host marking its own traffic, or a trust boundary that is not re-marking.
panels.title: DSCP class share of marked bytes

panels.description: A ranking over the raw flag string is monopolised by ack and psh,ack while the combinations that carry a diagnosis sit three orders of magnitude below it. Bucketing by outcome makes half-open connections, NULL scans and reset storms readable side by side. Clause order is load-bearing: reset is matched and excluded first, because an established bucket keyed on ack alone silently swallows rst,ack and every ECN variant of it. Measured in flow records, which are not sampling-multiplied, because a scan is measured in attempts rather than bytes. A bucket that is absent means the device reported no such combination.

targets.expr:
sum by (outcome) (
   label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags=~".*rst.*"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "reset seen", "", "")
or label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags=~".*syn.*",flags!~".*ack.*",flags!~".*rst.*"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "syn, never acked", "", "")
or label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags=~".*fin.*",flags!~".*ack.*",flags!~".*rst.*"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "fin, never acked", "", "")
or label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags="none"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "no bits set (NULL scan)", "", "")
or label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags=~".*syn.*",flags=~".*ack.*",flags!~".*rst.*"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "handshake (syn+ack)", "", "")
or label_replace(rate(xflow_tcp_flags_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",flags=~".*ack.*",flags!~".*rst.*",flags!~".*syn.*"}[$rollup_interval]), "outcome", "acked (established)", "", "")
)

panels.title: TCP handshake outcome

panels.description: A SYN flood is SYN records rising while SYN,ACK records do not follow. Two separate series rather than a quotient: a quotient renders as no data whenever either side is absent, and an absent flag combination must not be shown as a measured zero. The selectors match the ECN-negotiating variants a modern stack sends. Flow records, not sampling-multiplied. SYN,ACK exceeding bare SYN is expected under ingress-only observation.
panels.title: Half-open trend

panels.description: A country here is where the prefix is registered, not where the traffic went: a lab in Japan reaching an anycast prefix measures whichever continent that prefix is registered in. Not a figure to reconcile with a transit bill or a data-residency question. The union excludes private-to-private so LAN traffic does not occupy a panel about geography, and the ranked-bar form makes the per-country inbound and outbound asymmetry legible. Both directions appear as separate bars because observation is ingress-only. Packets are sampling-corrected.

targets.expr:
topk(12,
  sum by (src_country,dst_country) (rate(xflow_country_pair_packets_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src_country!="private"}[$rollup_interval]))
  or
  sum by (src_country,dst_country) (rate(xflow_country_pair_packets_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",dst_country!="private"}[$rollup_interval]))
)

panels.title: Remote countries by packets

panels.description: The half of the distributions module that had no panel. Duration distinguishes a circuit carrying long transfers from one carrying churn, and it is the direct read on whether the device's active and inactive flow timeouts are cutting records as configured. The p50 can collapse toward zero, which is native-histogram interpolation inside the lowest bucket where records whose two instants coincide pile up -- read p90 and p99. Only records that carried both instants contribute, so this histogram and the flow size one do not describe the same set.

targets.expr:
label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (exporter_address) (rate(xflow_flow_duration_seconds{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[$rollup_interval]))), "q", "p50", "", "") or
label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.90, sum by (exporter_address) (rate(xflow_flow_duration_seconds{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[$rollup_interval]))), "q", "p90", "", "") or
label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (exporter_address) (rate(xflow_flow_duration_seconds{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[$rollup_interval]))), "q", "p99", "", "")

panels.title: Flow duration percentiles

panels.description: The share of flow records shorter than one second: the honest reduction of the duration histogram to one number. A feed drifting toward all-short flows is either a scan or a device that has started emitting on its active timeout alone. Needs the distributions module; without it there is no series and the gauge is blank rather than zero.
panels.title: Short-lived flow share

panels.description: One of the few genuine time-series questions here: a fall in mean packet size is a workload shift or a fragmentation event, and it means something only against its own history. This is also the one volume-derived figure on the dashboard that is not an estimate -- the sampling correction cancels in the ratio. Framed against the 1500-byte MTU ceiling rather than an autoscaled axis, so a small wobble stays small.
panels.title: Mean packet size

panels.description: A threat hit is a discrete item to read and act on rather than a shape on a chart. The direction is the finding -- src is an inbound origin most lists name, dst means an inside host reached a listed destination, which is materially more serious. This family carries no address pair, so the address links through to the conversation tables. An empty table means no listed address was seen, which is not the same as clean.

value.title: Filter the conversation tables to this address

panels.title: Flagged addresses seen

panels.description: Scanning, with attribution. The TCP flags family can say a scan is happening but carries no address; the host pair table is the only path to who. A host jumping from tens to hundreds of distinct destinations is reconnaissance, malware, or a peer-to-peer client. Two bounds: the table is Top-K cut by byte volume, and a scan is low-volume by construction, so this is a floor on fan-out rather than a census; and it counts entries currently held, which the entry TTL scopes.
panels.title: Destination fan-out per LAN host

panels.description: One destination reached by many distinct sources is the shape of a flood target, and no volume panel shows it because a distributed flood is small per source by design. This counts breadth rather than summing bytes. Same two bounds as the fan-out panel: a Top-K cut by byte volume withholds low-volume sources first, and the entry TTL scopes it to entries currently held.
panels.title: Fan-in: sources per destination

panels.description: The classic reflection vectors, one row per destination and port, so a host answering these from outside is visible before it is conscripted into somebody else's attack. In a healthy network most of these ports produce no series at all, and that absence is the intended reading rather than a zero. Ranked by flow records, which are not sampling-multiplied. Observation is ingress-only: a row whose destination is inside the LAN is inbound traffic toward that service.
panels.title: UDP amplification exposure

panels.description: Five-tuples an inside host is using now and was not using over the preceding six hours: which machine changed behaviour, stated rather than inferred from a line chart. This is the only panel on the service five-tuple family, which is the single bridge from a host to an application or an AS, neither of which carries an address. Read as not seen recently rather than never seen -- an entry evicted at the entry TTL and recreated surfaces here on its own. Expect noise on a busy LAN.

targets.expr:
(
  group by (src, dst, proto, port) (rate(xflow_service_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",src=~"$focus"}[$rollup_interval]) > 0)
  or
  group by (src, dst, proto, port) (rate(xflow_service_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",dst=~"$focus"}[$rollup_interval]) > 0)
)
unless
(
  group by (src, dst, proto, port) (rate(xflow_service_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",src=~"$focus"}[6h] offset $rollup_interval) > 0)
  or
  group by (src, dst, proto, port) (rate(xflow_service_flows_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src=~"10\\..*|192\\.168\\..*|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\\..*",dst=~"$focus"}[6h] offset $rollup_interval) > 0)
)

panels.title: New service conversations

panels.description: Transit is billed on the 95th percentile of 5-minute samples. The inner range is pinned at five minutes -- the billing bucket rather than the dashboard's rollup -- with the subquery step matched to it, so each sample is one billing sample. Three caveats before this reaches a commercial conversation: it is a sampled estimate and an invoice is written from SNMP counters; it is computed over a Top-K bounded family, so it is the percentile of ranked traffic; and it spans the dashboard window, not the billing month.
panels.title: 95th percentile, 5-minute samples

panels.description: The aggregate percentile says what the circuit costs; this says who to talk to about it. Per-AS percentile on the same five-minute grid, so an AS that is large on average but flat drops below one that is spiky -- spikiness is what a percentile bill punishes, and this ordering genuinely inverts the mean-rate one. The per-AS values do not sum to the aggregate: percentiles are not additive, and reading this as a decomposition would be wrong. Same three caveats as the aggregate panel.

targets.expr:
topk(10, quantile_over_time(0.95, (sum by (dst_asn) (rate(xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other",src_asn="0",dst_asn!="0"}[5m])) * 8)[$__range:5m]))
* on (dst_asn) group_left (as_name)
  (
    label_replace(label_join(label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "dst_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", " (AS", "organization", "asn"), "as_name", "$1)", "as_name", "(.+)")
    or
    label_replace(group by (dst_asn) (xflow_asn_pair_bytes_total) unless on (dst_asn) label_replace(xflow_asn_info, "dst_asn", "$1", "asn", "(.+)"), "as_name", "AS$1", "dst_asn", "(.+)")
  )

panels.title: Who drives the 95th percentile

panels.description: Which counterparties carry enough traffic, in a balanced enough ratio, to be worth peering with directly instead of paying transit for. Read the ratio against the one a prospective peer publishes; most open policies accept roughly one to two. The guard on the ratio's denominator is load-bearing -- without it an AS seen inbound only renders as infinity. Joined rather than arithmetic: an AS seen in one direction only leaves a blank cell rather than a fabricated zero, and that asymmetry is real under ingress-only observation. Ranked from a Top-K bounded family, so this is the top of the peering picture rather than all of it.
panels.title: Peering candidates

panels.description: A domain is the device, protocol and domain identifier together, never the identifier alone: the three protocols number their domains independently, so one number from one device names as many domains as it speaks protocols. A template count and a sampling rate are small integers that change at reconfiguration rather than continuously, so a table is the right encoding and a mid-window change shows up as a changed cell. A domain that has declared no sampling rate leaves an empty cell rather than a zero or a one.
panels.title: Observation-domain inventory

panels.description: The fact that qualifies every composition panel on this dashboard. A table holding more entries than the Top-K bound publishes only the top ones and withholds the rest -- not folded into other, not summed anywhere. The cut is by byte volume descending, which is why every breadth and flow-count panel here carries the warning that a low-volume scanner can be withheld before it is ranked. Bound to the top_k variable rather than a literal, so a deployment that raises the flag does not read this panel wrong. A process-level measurement, correctly unfiltered by the exporter variable.
panels.title: Composition withheld by the Top-K bound

panels.description: When a device went silent and for how long, as a band per device rather than a sawtooth. The boolean comparison yields one and zero rather than filtering the series away, which is what a state panel needs. A device that stops exporting freezes every counter it feeds, which a rate renders as a flat zero indistinguishable from a quiet network; this band is what separates the two. The threshold is the entry TTL rather than an export cadence, so a device exporting only on a long idle timeout would flap here.
panels.title: Reception per device

panels.description: Every way a record can vanish before it becomes a series, on one bar list at real magnitudes. The distinction matters: drops and read errors are pre-decode, sequence loss happened on the wire and is the only cause that points at the network, decode rejects are post-receipt, and refusals are the exporter declining input by policy. One bar is not a lost record: past the device budget a sender keeps decoding into every aggregation table and loses only its own health series, which is the answer to a newly configured device whose traffic appears while its freshness never does. Fixed at one hour, matching the windows the alerting rules page on. Every other loss here bounds the accuracy of every composition panel above.

targets.expr:
sum by (cause) (
   label_replace(sum by (reason) (increase(xflow_receiver_dropped_packets_total[1h])), "cause", "receiver drop / $1", "reason", "(.+)")
or label_replace(sum by (reason) (increase(xflow_decode_errors_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[1h])), "cause", "decode reject / $1", "reason", "(.+)")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_sequence_missed_total{exporter_address=~"$exporter",exporter_address!="other"}[1h])), "cause", "export packets lost in transit", "", "")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_receiver_read_errors_total[1h])), "cause", "socket read error", "", "")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_exporters_refused_total[1h])), "cause", "device statistics dropped at the exporter budget", "", "")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_vendor_strings_refused_total[1h])), "cause", "vendor string refused", "", "")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_applications_refused_total[1h])), "cause", "application refused", "", "")
or label_replace(sum(increase(xflow_domains_refused_total[1h])), "cause", "observation domain refused", "", "")
)

panels.title: Records that never reached a series, last hour

panels.description: The set against its own 24-hour peak, beside the reload counters. A fetch that returned an error page loads a plausible-looking smaller set, which an absolute count cannot show. The ratio reads one both when the list is healthy and when it has simply never changed, which is why the reload counts sit beside it -- a healthy hourly loop and a cron job that died months ago are otherwise identical. Skipped lines measure the coverage the list does not have: a list published in CIDR notation loads only its bare addresses. A failed reload deliberately keeps the previous set, so a vanished list does not unflag every address at once.
panels.title: Threat list health

panels.description: Saturation of the decode path against the configured queue size. The queue fills before it drops, so this is the leading indicator for the queue_full bar in the loss panel and the reading to size against a Flexible NetFlow cache-flush storm. A process-level measurement: it carries no device label and is correctly unfiltered by the exporter variable.
panels.title: Receive queue depth

panels.description: What fraction of the records each database actually resolved: the direct answer to organization names or country codes not appearing. The denominator is filled plus unknown and deliberately excludes skipped, which means the device or an earlier source in the chain had already carried the dimension -- counting it as a failure would read a device exporting its own AS numbers as a broken database. The threat and mapping sources are excluded because their fill result is a hit rate against a hand-kept list rather than coverage, and any coverage threshold would read them permanently red. A falling figure over weeks is a stale database.
panels.title: Enrichment fill rate

panels.description: Records rejected for a template that has not arrived, on the window its own alerting rule uses and isolated from the other decode reasons, which the sibling rule deliberately excludes. After a restart this is expected and decays; a value that stays up is the signal to check the device's template refresh against the parser's template TTL. A device that never hit this condition has no series and no tile.
